content.overview: BNS s. 250 — Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment. BNS restatement of IPC 214. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 214. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 250 is the rule on “Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment”. The section provides that whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person, in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment shall,–. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 250 exists so that “Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment” has a closed legal test in Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Perjury, screening, harbouring, false charge, and failing to appear on a bond.

The provision in detail
250. Whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person, in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment shall,–

(a) if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;

(b) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine;

(c) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years, be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 250 (Taking gift, etc., to screen an offender from punishment), Chapter XIV — Of False Evidence and Offences Against Public Justice.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever accepts or attempts to obtain, or agrees to accept, any gratification for himself or any other person, or any restitution of property to himself or any other person, in consideration of his concealing an offence or of his screening any person from legal punishment for any offence, or of his not proceeding against any person for the purpose of bringing him to legal punishment shall,–
   (2) (a) if the offence is punishable with death, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine;
   (3) (b) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment for life, or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, and shall also be liable to fine;
   (4) (c) if the offence is punishable with imprisonment not extending to ten years, be punished with imprisonment of the description provided for the offence for a term which may extend to one-fourth part of the longest term of imprisonment provided for the offence, or with fine, or with both
Step 3 — Check limitations, provisos and the rest of the Chapter so you do not apply s. 250 in a vacuum.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 250 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
